chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَذَّانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَن عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا قَالُوا: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ إِذَا نَظَرَ إِلَى الْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارً مُقْبِلًا قَالَ: بَشِّرِ الْمُخْبِتِينَ وَكَانَ يَقُولُ: إِنَّ الْفُضَيْلَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ أَبِي وَإِنِّي لَأُحِبُّ الرَّجُلَ أَنْ يُحِبَّ أَصْحَابَ أَبِيهِ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a number of our companions who said: When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) used to look at al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar approaching, he would say: 'Give glad tidings to the humble,' and he used to say: 'Indeed, al-Fudhayl is from the companions of my father, and I love that a man loves the companions of his father.'

en.summary: This narration from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the spiritual status of al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar, linking his demeanor to the Quranic attribute of 'al-mukhbitin' (the humble/devout). It underscores the Shia concept of walayah, where the Imam’s affection for a companion is rooted in their love for the progenitor, thereby validating the chain of spiritual authority and companionship.
en.seo_question: What is the significance of al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar in Shia tradition according to Imam al-Sadiq?

key_terms.بَشِّرِ الْمُخْبِتِينَ: Give glad tidings to the humble (Quran 22:34)
key_terms.أَصْحَابِ أَبِي: The companions of my father (referring to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn or Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn's companions)
key_terms.الْفُضَيْلُ بْنُ يَسَارً: Al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar, a prominent companion of the Imams
